help.title: Guide
help.subtitle: Here you'll learn how the Method Archive is structured and how to use it for your participatory urban project – from finding the right method to running it.

steps.title: Find suitable methods
steps.text: On the home page, narrow down all methods with the filters – by participation depth, project phase, goal, format, duration, target group, group size and character. The search takes you straight to methods by name. Alternatively, the Method Assistant helps you choose in a dialogue.

steps.title: Get to know a method
steps.text: The detail page explains each method in full: its goal, the procedure across preparation, execution and evaluation, best-practice examples with images, and notes on when the method is useful – and when it isn't.

steps.title: Bookmark and compare
steps.text: Use the bookmark icon to collect interesting methods. Under “Bookmarked Methods”, a comparison table places their characteristics side by side – making the final choice easier.

steps.title: Export and share
steps.text: Print or save your selection as a PDF, or export it as a file – handy for coordinating within your team or as a handout for the session.

steps.title: Prepare and run
steps.text: The “Before you begin” checklist on the home page helps with preparation. Important: the time estimates refer to running the method with participants – preparation and follow-up take extra time.

pages.title: Method Archive
pages.text: The home page shows all methods. Use the filters and search to narrow them down by participation depth, target group, duration, goal, format and more until the right ones remain.

pages.title: Method Assistant
pages.text: The assistant helps you choose in a dialogue: describe your project in your own words – it suggests suitable methods from the archive and explains why they fit.

pages.title: Method detail page
pages.text: Every method has its own page with its goal, procedure (preparation, execution, evaluation), best-practice examples, tips and notes, plus related and follow-up methods. Use the bookmark icon to add it to your bookmarks.

pages.title: Bookmarked Methods
pages.text: Your bookmarked methods gather here in one place. A comparison table contrasts their characteristics; you can print the selection as a PDF or export it as a file and share it with your team.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.text: Via the accessibility icon you can adjust font size, high contrast, underlined links and reduced animations. The accessibility statement is linked in the footer.

pages.title: Contact
pages.text: Use the contact page to reach us – for example if a method is missing, you found an error, or you'd like to contribute to the archive.

faq.q: How do I find the right method?
faq.a: Use the filters and search on the home page. You can combine several criteria – the list updates instantly. If you'd rather choose in a dialogue, use the Method Assistant.

faq.q: What does the Method Assistant do – and what happens to my input?
faq.a: Based on your project description, the assistant suggests suitable methods from the archive and explains why they fit. To answer, your input is sent to an AI service – see the privacy policy for details.

faq.q: How do I bookmark a method?
faq.a: Click the bookmark icon on a method card or detail page. The method then appears under “Bookmarked Methods”.
Yes – they are stored locally in your browser. They won't be available on another device or after you clear your browser storage.

faq.q: Can I export or share my selection?
faq.a: Yes. Under “Bookmarked Methods” you can print or save your selection as a PDF, or export it as a file – handy for coordinating within your team.

faq.q: What do the methods' time estimates refer to?
faq.a: To actually running the method with participants. Preparation and follow-up take extra time and should be planned in separately.

faq.q: Is the archive available in English?
faq.a: Yes. Use the language switcher to switch between German and English at any time.

faq.q: How do I adjust font size and contrast?
faq.a: Open the settings via the accessibility icon and adjust font size, high contrast, underlined links and reduced animations.
Bookmarked methods and settings are stored only locally in your browser – no account needed. See the privacy policy and cookie policy for details.

faq.q: Who do I contact with questions?
faq.a: You can reach us directly via the contact page – we're happy to help.

help.footerText: Get in touch – we're happy to help.

beforeYouBegin.title: Before you begin
beforeYouBegin.item1: Ensure that all participants can communicate respectfully and on equal footing at every interaction.
beforeYouBegin.item2: Clarify in advance whether support services such as interpreters are needed so that all participants can follow and contribute to the discussion.
beforeYouBegin.item3:
You can ask participants to write their names and pronouns on a name tag or tape and wear it visibly. This can support a respectful, open, and welcoming atmosphere.
So always bring tape and markers.
beforeYouBegin.item4: Make sure you always have a way to take notes (laptop, tablet, pen and paper) to document discussions.
beforeYouBegin.item5: Suitable venue: sufficiently large room with good acoustics, seating available
beforeYouBegin.timeNote: The time indications for each method refer to the actual facilitation with participants. Preparation and follow-up require additional time.
